newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh begins talks with IMF on $600 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh begins talks with IMF on $600 mln loan.

text.p: Bangladesh, aiming to strengthen its foreign exchange coffers, has started talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on a $600 million concessional loan, government officials said on Sunday.
A six-member IMF team began preliminary discussions on the loan with the government on Saturday, officials with the finance ministry told Reuters.
The team, led by Margaret Kelly, adviser at the IMF's South East Asia and Pacific department, arrived here on Saturday.
The officials said the IMF team would review Bangladesh's economic situation and suggest areas of further reforms.

"Formal negotiations (on the loan) will begin only after the IMF team completes a report on its findings and sets conditons for the loan," said one official. "We are not in a hurry. The country is not in a balance of payment crisis at the moment ... We have to look at their (IMF's) terms."

Bangladesh's foreign exchange reserves have remained stagnant at around $2.0 billion over the past eight months, which is equal to import bills for over three months. The reserves were at $3.4 billion in April 1995.
"We are seeking the loan to strengthen the reserve position since we are planning further liberalisation of fiscal and exchange rules," a finance ministry official said.
Bangladesh has twice before received balance of payment support from the IMF, but only after agreeing to tough adjustment prescriptions.
The last IMF package, totalling $430 million in soft loans under the Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF), ended in 1993.
